column3: Kinetic Rain (the Changi airport sculpture): a grid of hundreds of polished droplets hanging on wires from the ceiling, seen in real 3D perspective from below-front, each droplet rising and falling on its own wire. Their heights form a living 3D relief, a rolling wave by default, that resolves into the numerals as raised (or lowered) regions, so the time is a sculpture of the whole field. The camera drifts slowly round the field so the depth is always felt; droplets catch a glint as they pass a height. On the minute a wave rolls across the field, dissolving the old digit and lifting the new one out of it. On the hour the whole field performs a big choreography (spiral, ripple from the centre, a twist) before settling into the new hour.

Trivision prism billboard: rows of vertical triangular prism slats in real 3D, each face carrying one third of a picture. The time is printed across the slats; on the minute the prisms rotate one after another in a cascading wave (each with spring overshoot and little shadows between them), revealing the new digit on the next face. Between turns the slats breathe and quiver, light sweeps across the faces as the whole billboard sways in perspective, and the prisms nudge a few degrees so the 3D is always alive. Design numerals that look printed for the slatted billboard (posterised, bold, with a glint where slats meet). The hour is a full-billboard show: prisms spin multiple turns in a wave across, or the billboard rotates in space.

Inflatable balloon numerals in real 3D: each digit is a shiny twisted-balloon shape (like balloon animals, or Jeff Koons' balloon sculptures): round tubes with pinched twists between segments, shaded by a light with a crisp specular highlight that slides as it turns, floating and bobbing in space, slowly yawing so you see they are round. Squash and stretch when they bump into each other. On the minute the old balloon is pricked or untwisted: it deflates with a wild fizzing spin flying around the screen (or untwists into a long tube), and a new tube is inflated and twisted segment by segment into the new numeral. On the hour a bunch of balloons floats up through the frame, or a big balloon carries the new hour in. Playful, bouncy, vivacious.

A rhythmic-gymnastics ribbon in real 3D: one long ribbon with a front face (lit) and back face (hatched or outlined), twisting, curling and flipping in space as a gymnast's stick (or an unseen hand) whirls it. The numerals are drawn by the ribbon itself, a continuous ribbon path that holds the shape of the time while it ripples and twists along its length, showing front and back as it turns. On the minute the ribbon unfurls from the old digit in a big swirling flourish (spirals, snakes, loops) and lays itself into the new digit. On the hour it performs a full routine (a helix, a spiral corkscrew across the screen) before forming the new hour. The hour and minutes may be two different ribbons or one ribbon with a knot.
